top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at Tour de Fukushima. Practice on rolling hills: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 87 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Tour de Fukushima's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
75ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Tour de Fukushima, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Tour de Fukushima. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 87, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
6,562ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Tour de Fukushima. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
6,562ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on rolling hills can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 87 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 6,562ft of climbing on rolling hills does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.weather: June in Hamadori coastal region, Fukushima Prefecture — Mild June coastal weather (15-25°C). Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks before Tour de Fukushima. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Tour de Fukushima’s 87 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Tour de Fukushima. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Tour de Fukushima rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on rolling hills to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 87 miles of rolling hills in Hamadori coastal region, Fukushima Prefecture.
